issue_context.title: MeshTexture behaves poorly when used as icon on Button
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

5ecd61a3150f87a433dd5a7ff49a842b72516640

### System information

Fedora Silverblue 36, Ryzen 2400G

### Issue description

There are several issues when using `MeshTexture` as icon in a `Button`.

* After assigning texture as icon, editor preview does not update until another unrelated property on button is changed
* Icon is completely misaligned
* `expand_icon` setting hides texture (or makes it zero size)

Demonstration:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/347965/182269987-3dcb56bc-2640-4202-a936-2772dc0547b5.mov



### Steps to reproduce

1. Add button
2. Assign a MeshTexture as icon

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: This is because the `changed` signal of the texture is not connected in `Button`.
Will work on a fix for this
The `expand_icon` part of this is covered by #59202

Found the same issue with TextureRect. Also it only updates when changing the TextureRect Visibility
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/120058545/2b16f6f3-0dd1-4d5f-85aa-e8381c127b80)

What version are you on? Because the changes to the texture updates the texture rect on all 4.x versions

So please open a new issue with clear reproduction steps for the issue and a minimum reproduction project
I found a similar issue with Godot 4.1 using TextureRect. I opened an issue https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81213

I just ran into this issue. I wanted a way to add a color to a texture button. I couldn't find a way to add color to a Texture2D so I tried using MeshTexture with a QuadMesh so I could use the material and color of the texture mesh. The same behavior described in Denis' post still occurs in Godot 4.3. As well as the TextureMesh ignores the QuadMesh's set material. It will only take the texture placed in the MeshTexture.

review_comments: It's not  a problem with this PR specifically as this was done in TextureProgressBar too, but DEV_ASSERT isn't very commonly used in the database. Maybe a `EFF_FAIL_COND` would be better for consistency ?
If you amend this PR, I think you can modify the test in `TextureProgressBar` too. I don't think we need another PR just for that. :)

The dev assert was used here, because it's internal method and null can only come from wrong usage. Dev assert checks are only done in dev builds AFAIK, null check in any other build is pointless in this case. The argument is property pointer.
That makes a lot of sense, restored the case
